recentItems.title: How Russian 'lies' about frontline led to Ukraine's biggest victory this year
recentItems.description:
How did Vladimir Putin announce a major military victory in Ukraine that never actually happened?

At the end of last month, the Russian president boldly claimed his forces had captured the strategic Ukrainian town of Sviatohirsk. The announcement seemed perfectly timed to rebut reports from the CIA that the invasion was failing. But there was one massive problem: it was a complete fabrication.

Days later, Ukrainian commanders filmed themselves casually strolling through the safe, sunny streets of Sviatohirsk, sending Russian military bloggers into a meltdown. So, who fed the Kremlin such inaccurate information?

recentItems.title: The shock Houthi mission to strangle global oil
recentItems.description:
In less than five days, Yemen’s Houthi fighters seized more than 2,600 square kilometres of coastline and pushed to within striking distance of one of the world’s most vital shipping lanes.

By Friday, the rebels had taken effective control of the approaches to the Bab el-Mandeb strait, the narrow gateway at the southern mouth of the Red Sea.

As oil prices surged and the offensive gathered pace, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman telephoned Donald Trump twice on Thursday, urging him to launch American strikes against the Houthis.

recentItems.title: How Ukraine Kept Its Biggest Victory of the Year a Secret | Unpacked
recentItems.description:
On Sept 1, Vladimir Putin gave no sign that he was aware a Ukrainian counter-attack was taking place in the Lyman direction.

He claimed that Moscow’s forces had captured 14 settlements in a steady advance over the past month, he claimed, “including… as of yesterday, the town of Sviatohirsk.”

If Putin had been correct about its capture, it would have marked an important staging point in his goal to seize the entirety of the Donbas.

But Putin had been badly misled.

recentItems.title: Trump refuses Saudi strike plea as Houthis seize Red Sea island & Gen Ben Hodges on US-Iran war
recentItems.description:
“The inability or unwillingness of the Trump administration to connect the dots on what is going on, from the Persian Gulf to the Red Sea, is a reflection of the lack of really good deep strategic thinking.”

On today’s episode of Iran: the Latest, Venetia Rainey is joined once again by former Commanding General of US Army Europe, Gen Ben Hodges, to discuss the US-Iran war as it nears the 200-day mark.

The Iran-backed Houthis have seized Yemen’s entire Red Sea coastline including the strategic Perim Island, giving them control of the vital Bab al-Mandeb Strait. And despite pleas from Saudi Arabia’s Mohammed bin Salman (MBS) to intervene as oil prices surge toward $110/barrel, Donald Trump has refused to launch strikes, offering up intelligence assistance instead. Gen Hodges analyses the strategic drift that has marked the war, the Pentagon and US policy in the Middle East. 

Plus, why mass lie-detector tests and personnel purges signal China-style paranoia inside the Pentagon, what news of damage to US fighter jets in Jordan says about US military preparedness, and the hard lessons from the Iraq and Afghanistan wars 25 years on from the 9/11 attacks.

recentItems.title: In full: Members of Parliament debate assisted dying bill
recentItems.description:
Friday’s vote on the assisted dying bill is an “extraordinary risk”, Labour MPs have said.

Dame Meg Hillier and Gareth Snell, who oppose and support assisted dying respectively, have written to parliamentary colleagues urging them not to wave through the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill.

The bill has been reintroduced to the Commons with only two small changes from Kim Leadbeater’s original legislation, which was backed by MPs but timed out in the Lords.

recentItems.title: 'Bombshell' claim that Netanyahu ignored UAE warning about Hamas October 7 attack
recentItems.description:
The Iran-backed Houthis have seized the strategic Red Sea port city of al-Mokha - apparently at the direction of the IRGC - as fighting in Yemen and Saudi Arabia escalates.  

On today’s episode of Iran: the Latest, Sophia Yan speaks to Jerusalem correspondent Henry Bodkin about the pressure the war is putting on the Bab al-Mandeb and Strait of Hormuz as oil prices pass the $100/barrel threshold for a second day. US President Donald Trump is clearly feeling the pressure, claiming the war will end following November’s midterm elections, and promising $5,000 cash payouts if Republicans retain Congress.

Plus, news that Iranian missile strikes damaged multiple US F-15 fighter jets in Jordan, Israeli leader Benjamin Netanyahu denies being warned about Hamas’s October 7 attack by the UAE, and MSF’S Charlene Silvin shares her first-hand experiences of wartime destruction in south Lebanon.
